contract: Read AGENTS.md, docs/README.md, docs/maintenance.md, docs/workers.md and owning topics before edits.
Use the superset-orchestrate skill. Coordinator assigns an isolated workspace, exact baseline, objective, acceptance criteria and verification commands before dispatch.
New user messages add requirements; they never silently cancel existing work. Record ownership, dependencies and pending work in docs/workers.md.
Coordinate shared renderer, settings and native hooks; do not broaden scope or overwrite other domains.
Builders may delegate one independent Superset critic and reuse it. Critics do not edit builder worktrees. At most three build/review/repair iterations per batch.
Capture revision, seed, viewport, settings and ordered input reproduction. Run meaningful checks; distinguish tests, rendered inspection, listening and physical device evidence.
Only root integrates main, publishes, restarts devices or changes production settings. Workers hand off exact commits, files, checks, limits and next ranked issues.
Keep topical Markdown within 120 lines where possible, maximum 150; index maximum 80. Replace stale requirements rather than appending logs.
Finish with SUPERSET_WORKER_DONE (task, summary, files, checks, handoff) or SUPERSET_WORKER_BLOCKED (task, reason, needs).
No recurring daemon is installed. After integration and explicit cleanup authorization, retire sessions and auxiliary workspaces; preserve evidence and role definitions in main.

Current product is Podrick’s Violin: base game with local owner controls, parchment/ink storybook UI and owner-provided cat artwork. Remove remote gameplay control; keep development asset updates. Recorded squeaks should dominate very quiet natural movement sounds.
